newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth to buy 49 pct of Nicaraguan wireless co.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth to buy 49 pct of Nicaraguan wireless co.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said Friday it had agreed to buy a 49 percent share in Telefonia Celular de Nicaragua (NICACEL), Nicaragua's only wireless telephone company. BellSouth said it will assume operational management of company and have an option to acquire an additional 40 percent of it.
Pending approval from the Nicaraguan government, BellSouth said it will pay an undisclosed amount to obtain a 49 percent stake in the company.
Current owners Carlos Reynaldo Lacayo, who will become NICACEL chairman, and Cesar Augusto Lacayo will own the remaining 51 percent of the company.

The NICACEL license covers Nicaragua's Pacific Region, an area with 2.4 million people, which includes the Nicaraguan capital of Managua and the heavily populated west coast area of the country. Under the terms of the license agreement, NICACEL has market exclusivity until July 1998.

BellSouth and its partners serve more than 8.5 million cellular customers worldwide, including 800,000 cellular customers in the Latin American countries of Argentina, Chile, Panama, Peru, Venezuela and Uruguay.
